headline: Medium-risk pair: shared MCP/API pathways create prompt-injection and cascading-error exposure; no direct filesystem overlap is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI is offline by default but exposes a Comfy API and file-based model surfaces; MemMachine uses an MCP Server and REST/Python SDK. No direct bridge is documented, so the pairwise injection path is inferred rather than proven. Because MemMachine can ingest external agent outputs through MCP and ComfyUI can emit workflow/content artifacts, the interaction is plausible but not default-dangerous.
conditions: IF MemMachine is configured to consume ComfyUI outputs via MCP or REST, prompt-like content can traverse the pair.
IF ComfyUI workflow or prompt text is forwarded into MemMachine without provenance tagging, injection risk increases.
mitigations: Disable any MCP route that ingests ComfyUI outputs.
Add a provenance prefix to all ComfyUI-generated text before passing it onward.
Review one sample workflow for instruction-like strings before enabling automation.
Keep the agents on separate queues or topics.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for all cross-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ComfyUI touches local media/model files and can run fully offline; MemMachine touches long-term user facts and conversational context and has allowlisted egress. The profiles do not show a shared workspace or shared principal, so leakage is not established. The main risk is manual or API-mediated transfer of sensitive context from MemMachine into ComfyUI prompts or outputs, which is limited and avoidable.
conditions: IF the same operator copies MemMachine context into ComfyUI prompts, sensitive facts may appear in generated media metadata or logs.
IF both agents are pointed at the same shared folder, local leakage risk rises.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Turn off verbose logging in both systems.
Avoid pasting conversational context into image prompts.
Check one generated artifact for embedded metadata before sharing.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, while MemMachine exposes MCP/REST but no write or git capability is listed. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The only plausible conflict is coordination around shared external resources if an orchestrator maps both agents onto the same mutable target, which is not documented here.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same downstream resource, conflicts can occur.
IF MemMachine is used to trigger actions that ComfyUI also updates indirectly, race conditions become possible.
mitigations: Keep ComfyUI read-only to its model directories.
Do not let MemMachine write into ComfyUI-managed paths.
Serialize any shared downstream updates manually.
Inspect one integration path for duplicate writes.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine can act as a user-facing agent over REST/MCP, so it may treat upstream content as authoritative. ComfyUI can generate outputs that look factual or structured, and if those outputs are fed into MemMachine without verification, errors can cascade into downstream travel-planning responses. The pairwise pathway is inferred, but the interaction is plausible in default integrations.
conditions: IF ComfyUI-generated text or captions are routed into MemMachine as facts, MemMachine may repeat them unverified.
IF MemMachine is configured to act on upstream outputs without a human review step, cascading errors can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review before MemMachine acts on ComfyUI output.
Mark all ComfyUI-derived text as untrusted.
Use a separate verification prompt before downstream use.
Sample one end-to-end run and inspect for factual drift.
requires-engineering: add confidence gating between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either open-source profile. ComfyUI is offline-capable and MemMachine uses allowlisted egress, so compliance risk is mainly operational rather than inherent. Because the profiles do not specify regulated data handling, the other agent is not cited beyond the pair context; there is no direct compliance breach shown.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is entered into MemMachine and then forwarded to ComfyUI logs or artifacts, retention concerns arise.
IF an operator stores EU or PHI data in either system without a policy, compliance gaps may appear.
mitigations: Do not enter regulated data unless policy is confirmed.
Review retention settings in both systems.
Delete one test artifact after verifying storage behavior.
Keep audit logs minimal.
requires-engineering: document data-flow and residency controls.
